rha_dataset.paper_title: Effect of Partial Replacement of OPC with Ghanaian Rice Husk Ash (RHA) on the Compressive Strength of Concrete
rha_dataset.rha_source_location: Asawaasi, Kumasi, Ashanti Region, Ghana (uncontrolled burning <400C)
rha_dataset.output_availability: partial (only some 28d values in text; full RHA0-25% x 3-180d matrix only in Figs 6-9)
rha_dataset.notes: RHA 0/5/10/15/20/25% tested for grades C20/C25/C30/C35 at 3/7/14/21/28/56/90/180d, but only the listed 28d control & 5% values are given numerically; rest in figures. w/c 0.45 all mixes. Rapid Hardening PC 42.5; river sand + crushed granite. No kg/m3 proportions (DOE mix). Intro cites Obilade (2014) Nigerian RHA values -> see Cited_sources.
rha_dataset.evidence: '28 day strength of the control concrete for C20 and C25 were 21.8 and 30.5 N/mm2 ... C30 and C35 ... 28.1 and 32.8'; '5% RHA for C20 ... 21.8 to 22.2 ... C25 30.5 to 29.5'. w/c 0.45.

rha_dataset.notes: Concrete mix ratio 1:2:4, w/c 0.55, 90 samples, cured 7 & 28d. Compressive & split tensile strengths reported ONLY as % change vs control in Figs 4-5 (no absolute MPa, no kg/m3). Needs figure digitization. RHA & FA each in equal proportion.
rha_dataset.evidence: 'mix proportions of 1:2:4 and 0.55 water/cement ratio ... 5%RHA+5%FA compressive strength enhanced by 16.14% ... split tensile improved 15.20% vs control at 28d'.
